members.text:
# One DHS People, Access and Culture — Build-Ready Master PRD

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Version | 2.2 Master (build-ready export) |
| Date | September 4, 2026 |
| Status | Complete enough to proceed outside this platform |
| Owner / practice owner | Gary Banks — Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant |
| Bar | New build must score **90–95 / 100** on operational sophistication (prior live refs scored ~74 and ~71) |

---

## 0. Bottom line (read this first)

**What you are building:** A self-directed DHS staff resource program that scales Gary’s Equity & Inclusion Operations consulting practice. Assist; do not babysit. Meet inexperienced staff where they are; graduate them to independent equity execution. Seeds and fertilizer; they water the garden.

**What it is not:** A clone of the current live apps. A performative content hub. A personal chatbot. A case/HR/surveillance system. A Cursor Origin project (delivery is **GitHub + Vercel cloud** from Gary’s PC).

**Visual brand floor:** Color/type/hero language from `https://one-dhs-equity-resource.vercel.app/` (navy `#003865`, green `#78be21`, Aptos). Harvest useful structure/content from that app **and** `https://one-dsd-resource-hub-live.vercel.app/`. Do not rebuild either architecture.

**Primary IA call:** Lead with **Guided Start + graduation paths**. Keep Four Doors (Foundation / Learn / Apply / Lead) as a secondary map, not the spine.

**Human job vs app job:** Gary embeds equity into programs at conceptual/launch stage (face-to-face/calendar). The app is private Ask, Community Intelligence (US + global with Minnesota focus), knowledge/tools, structured consult intake queue, and capability transfer.

**Success:** Staff can do ordinary equity work without the consultant. Consult queue gives Gary heads-up before meetings. Score 90–95 on the operational bar.

---

## 1. Locked decisions (this conversation)

1. Target score **90–95/100** (not mid-70s content hubs).
2. Delivery: **GitHub + Vercel (cloud host)**; develop from Gary’s PC; **not** Cursor Origin.
3. Color from One DHS live; patterns from both live apps; new agentic architecture.
4. Guided Start + graduation paths primary; Four Doors secondary.
5. Mindset twin / orchestrator role = **Equity & Inclusion Operations Consultant** (digital practice twin), not a staff-facing persona brand. Staff brand = **One DHS Support**.
6. Build swarm roles: E&I Ops Consultant (orchestrator), Prototyper, Instructional Designer, Senior AI Engineer, Cross-Cultural Researcher (US+world, Minnesota focus), Product/Program Evaluator, Accessibility & Plain Language, Content Knowledge Steward, Security/Privacy Guardian, Facilitation & Coaching Specialist.
7. In-product agents (app layer): Orchestrator, Ask Concierge, Community Intelligence Guide, Resource Librarian, Plain-Language & A11y Reviewer, Consultation Intake & Queue, Learning/Graduation Coach, Program Embed Advisor; near-term Content Sentinel, Eval/Model Steward. MVP autonomy **A0–A2**.
8. Hard safety: no case/PII, no surveillance/ranking, no autonomous publish, no icon-only staff UI, no invented Official law/policy.
9. Anti-performative; capability transfer KPIs, not chat volume.

---

## 2. Early-2027 MUST (ship slice)

- Home (One DHS brand, hero, Guided Start)
- Ask (private text Q&A + escalate to consult)
- Minnesota Communities / Community Intelligence (progressive briefs + work handoff; US/global with MN focus)
- Resources / library (search, layers, guides)
- Consultation intake + queue + practice-owner heads-up packet (manual calendar MVP)
- Graduation paths for: new program concept; policy/form/notice; community engagement; workplace climate (non-HR); facilitation session
- Accessibility baseline WCAG 2.2 AA; staff copy brand pass
- Adaptive Program Intelligence scaffold: model registry stub, agent definitions, tool adapters, governed memory, eval harness placeholders
- Standard/My View local only (no name/email profile to vendor)

**Defer:** full ecosystem scoreboards, A3+ autonomy, auto calendar invites, consultant admin console clone, multi-admin enterprise analytics.

---

## 3. Companion specs (same pack — use together)

| Doc | Path |
| --- | --- |
| Product PRD v2.1 (full) | `One-DHS-People-Access-and-Culture-Product-PRD-v2.md` / `.docx` |
| Ask MVP Contract | `One-DHS-Ask-MVP-Contract.md` |
| Community Intelligence MVP Contract | `One-DHS-Community-Intelligence-MVP-Contract.md` |
| Agentic Tools Catalog | `One-DHS-Agentic-Tools-Catalog.md` / `.docx` |
| Consultation Intake & Queue | `One-DHS-Consultation-Intake-and-Queue.md` / `.docx` |
| Graduation Paths | `One-DHS-Graduation-Paths.md` / `.docx` |
| TRD Adaptive Program Intelligence | `One-DHS-TRD-Adaptive-Program-Intelligence.md` / `.docx` |
| Staff Copy & Brand Pass | `One-DHS-Staff-Copy-and-Brand-Pass.md` / `.docx` |
| Canonical Source Freeze | `One-DHS-Canonical-Source-Freeze.md` / `.docx` (update: canonical write target = new GitHub `one-dhs-pac`, not Origin) |

---

## 4. 90–95 scorecard (release bar)

To clear 90–95, the build must beat prior apps on:

| Dimension | Prior weakness | Pass condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Operational scale | Content hub, not consultant scale layer | Ask → artifact → independence → optional consult is real |
| Capability transfer | Consumption metrics | Graduation evidence without employee ranking |
| Agentic depth | Little/no governed agents | Registry, tools, evals, A0–A2 with human gates |
| Work context | Generic or DSD-only | Agencywide + harvest DSD role/work patterns |
| Safety & trust | Variable | Hard refusals, boundaries, plain brand |
| Visual craft | Good on One DHS live | Match One DHS color/type/hero quality |
| Performance/reliability | Some 500s on sibling staging | Primary journeys green; browser-flow gates |

---

## 5. Next steps if continuing elsewhere

1. Create private GitHub repo `one-dhs-pac`; push from Gary’s PC; connect Vercel project.
2. Implement MUST slice against companion contracts.
3. Seed corpus from approved harvest (not auto-canonical).
4. Run must-pass evals (Ask, CI, intake, graduation, a11y).
5. Re-score against §4 before calling it done.

---

## 6. Full Product PRD v2.1 body

The following is the full Product PRD v2.1 text, which remains the detailed product contract. Sections 0–5 above are the export overlay of locked decisions.


# One DHS People, Access and Culture — Product PRD v2.1

**Staff-facing product contract for the DHS equity infrastructure ecosystem**

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Version | 2.1 |
| Date | September 4, 2026 |
| Status | Proposed product baseline reflecting owner framing |
| Program owner | One DHS People, Access and Culture Program |
| Principal architect / practice owner | Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant (Gary Banks) |
| Initial operating context | Minnesota DHS; DSD as originating and proving environment |
| Audience for this document | Product owner, Equity Directors, build leads, reviewers |

---

## 0. How to use this document

**What this PRD is**

- The product contract for the staff-facing One DHS People, Access and Culture (PAC) layer.
- The freeze of Early-2027 MVP scope versus deferred work.
- The authority map for what the product may and may not do.

## 1. One-page product definition

**Human responsibility first.** The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant (principal architect) is brought into scoping and goals when a staff member has a program launching or in conceptual stage, and advises how to embed and infuse equity considerations in the work. Face-to-face and calendar consults remain available; the application does not replace them.

**Product decision.** Build a self-service / self-directed resource program that scales that practice across ~180 DSD staff personally, ~4,000 agencywide, and ~39 partners — without babysitting. The application assists, seeds, and fertilizes; staff water the garden and graduate toward independent equity execution. One DHS PAC is the staff-facing delivery layer. Equity Director pilots are the path for administration learning and phased scale.

**What the application encodes.** Operational equity judgment from Equity and Inclusion Operations practice — a governed digital simulation of that practice, not a fake persona chatbot. Staff-facing brand remains **One DHS Support / resource program**. The Mindset Twin is internal, governed, and reviewable operating judgment — never the public product identity and never a substitute for human authority.

**Reject performative equity.** Meet inexperienced staff where they are; graduate capability. Provide a private, low-shame path for introverts and for people uncomfortable asking a person of color in management or DEIA roles — Ask, community intelligence, and knowledge tools first; optional human consult when needed.

| Layer | What it is | What staff see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Ecosystem** | Shared standards, partnership spine, tool portfolio, governance, evaluation | Shared program identity and commitments |
| **Staff Program** | Self-directed Ask, community intelligence, knowledge base, learning, tools, observances, consult handoff | Home, Guided Start, Ask, Learn, Minnesota Communities, Resources, Support / Consult |
| **Practice Workspace** | Protected workflows for authorized practitioners; consultation intake queue for the practice owner | Consultation, analysis, facilitation, work products |
| **Mindset Twin** | Encoded Equity and Inclusion Operations judgment under governance and human review | Not branded as a personal chatbot; appears only as assistive workflows with clear human gates |

**Thesis.** If DHS combines human consultative leadership, a self-directed scale layer, Equity Director stewardship, governed knowledge, accessible learning, practical workflows, partnership infrastructure, and a controlled reasoning layer, the agency can increase the reach and durability of equity practice without flattening local authority, replacing human accountability, or performing equity theater.

**Partnership spine (non-negotiable).** Equity is everyone's work · Build on existing infrastructure · Center lived experience · Follow the data · Move at the speed of trust · Work in partnership.

### 8.1 Self-directed resource paths

The staff program scales Equity and Inclusion Operations practice through four complementary paths. Face-to-face and calendar consults remain available; the application assists and does not replace them.

| Path | Staff value | Product rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Ask** | Private, low-shame questions on policy, practice, intercultural competence, access, and workplace culture | Early-2027 MUST. Answer with governed knowledge; show uncertainty; never invent authority; escalate when human judgment is required |

**Graduation stance.** Meet inexperienced staff where they are. Reject performative checkbox equity. Success is staff who can embed equity considerations in their own launches with less repeated dependency on the same human consultant for comparable work.

## 9. Equity Director pilot model (compact)

Equity Directors lead administration pilots. Pilots do not decide whether the agencywide program exists; they decide how the shared program is contextualized, supported, improved, and scaled.

| Responsibility | Program owner provides | Equity Director leads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Readiness | Standards, platform, content baseline, accessibility evidence, pilot package | Local sponsor alignment, participant scope, risks, readiness |
| Implementation | Pathways, facilitation tools, support, technical operations | Local sequencing, communication, facilitation, adaptation within boundaries |
| Evaluation | Common measures, instruments, privacy rules, analysis support | Context interpretation, participant protection, local learning, recommendations |
| Scale decision | Cross-pilot synthesis, remediation plan, agencywide options | Administration disposition and conditions for expansion |

**Pilot decision standard.** Staff can find trusted support faster, understand how to use it, apply it to real work, and identify when human authority is required. The pilot also produces actionable evidence about inaccessible, outdated, missing, confusing, or difficult-to-apply elements.

## 10. Adaptive Program Intelligence (product expectations)

The program is an adaptive platform: the intelligence layer can improve as models and tools improve, without rebuilding the application. It must evolve continuously but not drift casually. Agentic behavior should be ambitious inside bounded self-service workflows (Ask, triage, classification, accessibility review, consult prep) — not timid content search only — while remaining within tool boundaries and human gates.

| Expectation | Product meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Model evolution | Approved models are registered with purpose, scope, cost/risk notes, and which agents may use them. Switching models does not require rewriting staff routes |
| Agent definitions | Each agent has purpose, allowed inputs/outputs, scope, review rule, evaluation test, and enabled/disabled state |
| Evaluations | New models are judged on program tasks: accuracy, scope adherence, plain language, accessibility checks, no surveillance behavior, human-gate respect — not on impressiveness |
| Upgrade pathway | Candidate → evaluation cases → compare → sandbox → limited pilot → owner review → enable / hold / reject |
| Durable program memory | Preserve approved decisions, review outcomes, content history, scope rules, published versions, accepted/rejected recommendations, evaluation results — not loose chat residue |
| Tool boundaries | Agents may draft, classify, check accessibility, prepare agendas, summarize de-identified themes. Agents may not publish, send official messages, make HR/legal decisions, handle complaints, act on case data, rank staff, or change another administration's content |

Detail for adapters, prompt versioning, feature flags, and eval harness belongs in the TRD.

## 11. Mindset twin — product role, first three workflows, autonomy rules

### 11.1 Product role

The mindset twin is a protected operating reasoning layer: the **encoded operating judgment of the Equity and Inclusion Operations practice** (the principal architect's method), governed and reviewable. It is a digital simulation of that practice under governance — **not** a fake persona chatbot, **not** a named substitute for a person of color in management/DEIA roles, and **not** the public identity of the staff program. Staff-facing brand remains One DHS Support / resource program.

It helps authorized users sense, analyze, design, plan, prepare, review, evaluate, and improve bounded work under human authority. Stance: systems-oriented, people-focused, humble, discreet, evidence-humble, anti-performative, and able to work through bureaucracy without being captured by it.

### 11.2 First three workflows (must-pass intent)

| Workflow | Must-pass intent | Autonomy ceiling at launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **(a) Resource classification** | Correctly classify resource type, audience, authority status, currency, and review need; surface uncertainty; never invent authority | A2 Produce drafts; human confirms classification before publication impact |
| **(b) Plain-language and accessibility review** | Flag unclear language, missing structure, contrast/alt/caption risks, and inaccessible interaction patterns; propose remediations; never claim WCAG pass without evidence | A2 Produce review drafts; human owns release disposition |
| **(c) Consultation triage / agenda prep** | First-class intake/queue: structured questions (program stage, goals, equity embed asks, desired outcome) so the practice owner gets heads-up before meetings; propose agenda with owners and timeboxes; escalate when human judgment is required; never decide the consultation outcome | A2 Produce agenda/intake drafts; A3 only for reversible routing/scheduling with undo |

### 11.3 Autonomy ladder (earned)

| Level | Agent authority | Required control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A0 Observe | Read, classify, summarize, detect patterns | Visible activity; no external action |
| A1 Recommend | Propose questions, options, learning, next steps | Designated human chooses |
| A2 Produce | Create complete editable drafts and artifacts | Human edit / approve / reject / regenerate |
| A3 Execute reversible | Save, organize, route, schedule, update state, run checks | Undo, pause, limits, activity history |
| A4 Run bounded workflow | Complete a predefined multi-step process within limits | Approval gates, exception review, rollback |
| A5 Propose adaptation | Candidate behavior or content improvements from evidence | Only program owner promotes to production |

Autonomy percentages are aspirations, not release requirements. Success is safe, useful completion and appropriate escalation.

## 12. Content and accessibility standards (compact)

| Standard | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Accessibility target | WCAG 2.2 AA and applicable Section 508 expectations across staff, contributor, owner, and generated artifacts |
| No-icons rule | Staff-facing interfaces contain no icon, pictogram, or symbol-only control, progress, or navigation indicators |
| Canonical content | One content object governs all renditions (web, Word, PDF, slides, audio, video) with ID, version, owner, authority status, review date, language, accessibility status |
| Owner admissibility | System may surface missing context; only the designated human owner publishes, qualifies, revises, holds, or rejects |
| Migration rule | Existing One DSD artifacts are migration inputs, not automatic approval, authority, or accessibility proof. Preserve useful substance; require explicit human disposition. Missing context never auto-removes an item |
| Representation | Medium alone (including AI-assisted imagery) does not decide approval. Purpose, rights, realism, context, accessibility, representational risk, and owner decision govern. Photorealistic synthetic imagery must not be presented as documentary evidence of a real person, event, or community |
| Interactive learning | Keyboard and assistive-technology paths required; drag tasks need non-drag alternatives |
| Generated artifacts | Word, PDF, PowerPoint, Excel, audio, video must meet accessibility requirements before publication or formal delivery |

## 14. Ecosystem intelligence — product constraints for later phases

MVP may provide a structured asset inventory, audited resource measures, domain capability profiles, and descriptive network maps under pilot-ready rules (Section 7.2).

**Refused always (including Phase 3+):**

- Composite maturity / enterprise scores
- Fake causal ratios (including disparities-addressed ÷ disparities-identified)
- Personnel ranking or performance scorecards from ecosystem data
- Public leaderboards of administrations or programs
- Automated funding or program decisions
- Gap/duplication flags from network degree alone
- Tribal affiliation inference; Nation-governed data without documented authority

**Phase 3+ constraints (summary — full ECO-* registry lives in Operating Model / TRD / Knowledge Map, not this PRD):**

| Constraint family | Product rule |
| --- | --- |
| Evidence labeling | Descriptive, associative, contribution, and causal claims stay distinct; unsupported causal language blocked in publication |
| Capability domains | Separate evidence-based domains; dual-rating and agreement thresholds before comparative release |
| Resources | Direct / embedded / shared / pass-through / contracted stay distinct; ratios never become performance proxies alone |
| Network | Typed, temporal edges; corroboration required before gap or duplication findings |
| Privacy / Tribal | Field-level authority before ingestion; Tribal features disabled until consultation and agreements exist |
| Human disposition | Every consequential finding links to investigate / connect / support / sustain / redesign / scale / discontinue with owner and review date |

## 18. Definition of done for Phase 1

Phase 1 is done when **all** of the following are true:

1. Sections 7.1 MUST items are implemented and demonstrated in the running application.
2. STAFF-01 through STAFF-11 acceptance criteria pass moderated review.
3. KPI-01 through KPI-12 either pass or have an explicit owner-approved exception with remediation date (exceptions cannot waive Ownership or prohibited-PII gates).
4. Mindset workflows (a)–(c) pass must-pass suites; no other protected intelligent workflows are enabled in production.
5. Accessibility, security/privacy, and operations release gates pass.
6. Decision log items D-02, D-11, and D-12 are either closed or explicitly blocked from enterprise claims.
7. Migration dispositions exist for priority One DSD / One DHS artifacts included in launch content.
8. Rollback target is named and recovery rehearsal succeeded.

The program is not “done” because every future feature exists. It is ready to scale when people can do better work, authority remains human and explicit, and improvement compounds through evidence rather than drift.

**v2.0 → v2.1 (owner framing, September 4, 2026).** §1 rewritten to lead with human consultative role + self-directed scale layer; §8.1 Self-directed resource paths (Ask, community intelligence, knowledge base, optional consult) added; Ask and Community Intelligence locked into Early-2027 MUST; consultation intake/queue made first-class; capability-transfer outcomes and KPIs added; Mindset Twin clarified as encoded Equity and Inclusion Operations judgment (not a personal chatbot); Adaptive Program Intelligence gains ambitious-but-bounded agentic expectation. Structure otherwise unchanged from v2.0.

| v1.2 area | v2.x treatment |

| §1 Executive product definition | §1 One-page product definition; four-layer split; v2.1 human+scale framing |
| §2 Problem / partnership spine / domains / leverage | §2 tight problem table; spine kept; domain/leverage detail → Operating Model / Knowledge Map |
| §3 North-star outcomes | §4 retained; v2.1 adds capability transfer |
| §4 Program architecture | §3 Product portfolio map |
| §5 Boundaries | §5 retained and sharpened; v2.1 anti-performative / not-persona rows |
| §6 Audiences | §6 retained; v2.1 adds Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant |
| §7 Agencywide components / practice principles | Summarized into §1–§4; full principle tables → Operating Model |
| §8 Staff experience | §8 Phase 1 + §8.1 self-directed paths (v2.1) |
| §9 Equity Director pilot | §9 compact |
| §10 Equity-practice workflows | Deferred detail → Practice Workspace backlog; consultation intake in §7.1 / §8.1 / §11 |
| §11–§13 Mindset twin / autonomy / MIND-* | §11 + autonomy ladder; encoded practice judgment clarified in v2.1; MIND detail → TRD / eval suites |
| §14–§15 Content / representation | §12 compact; CNT/EDIT/HR IDs → Knowledge Map / TRD |
| §16–§17 Governance / ownership gate | §15–§16; ownership softened as unresolved hard gate |
| §18 Accessibility | §12 |

| §24–§25 Launch minimum / release gates | §7 + §15 |

| Adaptive Program Intelligence (post-v1.2 direction) | §10; v2.1 ambitious-within-bounds sentence |

# One DHS PAC — Handoff Roadmap Through First Code

**Audience:** Regular Grok (handoff from Prototyper / Grok Bot session with Gary Banks)  
**Date:** September 4, 2026  
**Definition of first code:** Step **B4** complete — repo scaffolded, tokens + hero committed and pushed, **Vercel preview URL** live.

Use the export pack. Do not rediscover product locks. Do not use Cursor Origin.

---

## A. DONE (locked — do not reopen)

### Product framing locks
| Lock | Decision |
|------|----------|
| Product scale | Self-directed scale of E&I consulting (digital twin practice, not a thin chatbot) |
| Quality bar | **90–95 / 100** target score |
| Delivery | **GitHub + Vercel** (cloud). **Not** Cursor Origin |
| Color / visual system | From **one-dhs-equity-resource** |
| Reference harvest | Patterns from **both** live apps (equity resource + DSD hub / twin surface) |
| Primary UX path | **Guided Start + graduation** primary |
| Research / CI lens | Cross-cultural intelligence: **US + world**, **Minnesota** focus |
| Orchestrator role | **Equity & Inclusion Ops Consultant** (mindset twin / digital practice twin) |
| Staff-facing brand | **One DHS Support** (not the orchestrator persona name) |
| Origin | **Cancelled** — do not create or resume Origin repos for this product |

### Export zip docs (all in `One-DHS-PAC-Export-2026-09-04/`)
- `README.md`
- `One-DHS-PAC-Build-Ready-Master-PRD.md` / `.docx`
- `One-DHS-People-Access-and-Culture-Product-PRD-v2.md` / `.docx`
- `One-DHS-PRD-v2.1-change-summary.md`
- `One-DHS-Canonical-Source-Freeze.md` / `.docx`
- `One-DHS-Reference-Harvest-Brief.md` / `.docx`
- `One-DHS-Ask-MVP-Contract.md`
- `One-DHS-Community-Intelligence-MVP-Contract.md`
- `One-DHS-Ask-and-CI-MVP-Contracts.docx`
- `One-DHS-Consultation-Intake-and-Queue.md` / `.docx`
- `One-DHS-Graduation-Paths.md` / `.docx`
- `One-DHS-Staff-Copy-and-Brand-Pass.md` / `.docx`
- `One-DHS-TRD-Adaptive-Program-Intelligence.md` / `.docx`
- `One-DHS-Agentic-Tools-Catalog.md` / `.docx`
- `reference-assets/` (screenshots + logos + hero images)
- This handoff: `One-DHS-PAC-Handoff-Roadmap-Through-First-Code.md` / `.docx`

### Swarm agents listed (build + in-product)
**Build swarm roles:** E&I Ops Consultant (orchestrator), Prototyper, Instructional Designer, Senior AI Engineer, Cross-Cultural Researcher (US+world, MN focus), Product/Program Evaluator, Accessibility & Plain Language, Content Knowledge Steward, Security/Privacy Guardian, Facilitation & Coaching Specialist.

**In-product agents (app layer):** Orchestrator, Ask Concierge, Community Intelligence Guide, Resource Librarian, Plain-Language & A11y Reviewer, Consultation Intake & Queue, Learning/Graduation Coach, Program Embed Advisor; near-term Content Sentinel, Eval/Model Steward. MVP autonomy **A0–A2**.

---

## B. REMAINING BEFORE FIRST CODE (do in order)

1. **Source freeze — GitHub repo:** Confirm / create the canonical GitHub repository for One DHS PAC (empty or agreed starter). Record owner/name and default branch.
2. **Vercel connect:** Connect that GitHub repo to Vercel (project created, Git integration on). No Origin.
3. **Harvest scope lock:** Finalize what is in-scope to harvest from both live apps (IA patterns, components, copy tone, flows) vs out-of-scope chrome.
4. **Ask MVP open freezes:** Close remaining Ask contract open items (routing, grounding, refusal, handoff to intake).
5. **CI MVP open freezes:** Close Community Intelligence open items (MN/US/world framing, sources, output shapes).
6. **Intake open freezes:** Close consultation intake / queue open fields, SLAs, staff vs public paths.
7. **Graduation open freezes:** Close Guided Start → graduation path definitions and exit criteria.
8. **Brand / staff copy open freezes:** Close One DHS Support naming, hero, CTAs, plain-language pass leftovers.
9. **Canonical source freeze sign-off:** Treat Canonical Source Freeze + Master PRD as the single build truth; note any last deltas only here.
10. **Architecture A0:** System context diagram (surfaces, agents, data stores, auth boundary).
11. **Architecture A1:** Next.js app router map + API / agent invocation boundaries for A0–A2 autonomy.
12. **Architecture A2:** Env, secrets, model/provider stubs, logging/eval hooks (no production secrets in repo).
13. **Next.js stack lock:** App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind (or agreed tokens pipeline), agreed UI kit, lint/format, test runner.
14. **Design tokens from equity-resource:** Extract color / type / spacing tokens into repo-ready CSS variables or Tailwind theme.
15. **Bootstrap repo scaffold:** `create-next-app` (or agreed template) with folders for `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `agents/` stubs, `content/`.
16. **Tokens commit:** Commit design tokens + base layout shell.
17. **Hero commit:** One DHS Support hero + Guided Start entry (static/MVP shell) matching brand pass.
18. **Push to GitHub:** Push main (or agreed branch) to the connected repo.
19. **Vercel preview deploy:** Trigger deploy from push; capture preview URL.
20. **B4 gate — first code declared:** Preview URL verified; handoff note updated with URL + commit SHA.

**First code = B4 done** = steps **1–20** complete with a live **Vercel preview URL**.

Suggested micro-labels (optional): treat **15–20** as the B4 bootstrap burst (scaffold → tokens → hero → push → preview → declare).

---

## C. AFTER FIRST CODE — MUST features

Implement next (order flexible within this set, but all are MUST before calling MVP “feature-complete”):

- **Ask** — working Ask surface per Ask MVP contract
- **CI** — Community Intelligence library / guide surface per CI MVP contract
- **Library** — Resource library / librarian path
- **Intake** — Consultation intake + queue
- **Graduation** — Guided Start + graduation paths
- **Agent stubs** — In-product agent stubs wired at A0–A2 (orchestrator + listed agents)
- **A11y** — Accessibility & plain-language pass (keyboard, contrast, semantics, plain language)
- **Rescore** — Re-score against 90–95 bar; close gaps

---

## D. Open Gary questions (5)

1. Exact **GitHub org/user + repo name** for the canonical PAC repo?
2. Preferred **Vercel team/project name** and any existing project to attach vs create new?
3. Any **auth / SSO** constraint for first preview (public preview OK vs staff-only)?
4. Which of the two live apps is **primary** when harvest patterns conflict (equity-resource vs DSD hub)?
5. Model / provider preference for Ask + orchestrator stubs in first vertical slice (and any must-not-use list)?

---

## E. Instruction to Regular Grok

1. **Use the export zip** (`One-DHS-PAC-Export-2026-09-04.zip` and folder of the same name). Start from Master PRD + Canonical Source Freeze + this roadmap.
2. **Do not rediscover** product framing locks in section A. Treat them as closed.
3. **No Origin.** Delivery is GitHub + Vercel only.
4. **Finish B (1–20)** through first code (preview URL), then execute **C** MUST features.
5. Prefer closing Gary’s five open questions early if they block B1–B2; otherwise proceed with documented assumptions and flag them.

---

*End of handoff roadmap — through first code generation.*

members.text:
# One DHS People, Access and Culture — Product PRD v2.1

**Staff-facing product contract for the DHS equity infrastructure ecosystem**

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Version | 2.1 |
| Date | September 4, 2026 |
| Status | Proposed product baseline reflecting owner framing |
| Program owner | One DHS People, Access and Culture Program |
| Principal architect / practice owner | Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant (Gary Banks) |
| Initial operating context | Minnesota DHS; DSD as originating and proving environment |
| Audience for this document | Product owner, Equity Directors, build leads, reviewers |

---

## 0. How to use this document

**What this PRD is**

- The product contract for the staff-facing One DHS People, Access and Culture (PAC) layer.
- The freeze of Early-2027 MVP scope versus deferred work.
- The authority map for what the product may and may not do.

**What this PRD is not**

- Not the Operating Model (roles, cadence, partnership routines).
- Not the Technical Requirements Document (TRD: schemas, adapters, model registry internals, eval harness).
- Not the Knowledge Map (content inventory, semantic graph, migration catalog).
- Not a legal agreement, Tribal consultation record, or enterprise sponsorship package.

Point those companion documents here for product intent; do not paste their internals into this PRD.

---

## 1. One-page product definition

**Human responsibility first.** The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant (principal architect) is brought into scoping and goals when a staff member has a program launching or in conceptual stage, and advises how to embed and infuse equity considerations in the work. Face-to-face and calendar consults remain available; the application does not replace them.

**Product decision.** Build a self-service / self-directed resource program that scales that practice across ~180 DSD staff personally, ~4,000 agencywide, and ~39 partners — without babysitting. The application assists, seeds, and fertilizes; staff water the garden and graduate toward independent equity execution. One DHS PAC is the staff-facing delivery layer. Equity Director pilots are the path for administration learning and phased scale.

**What the application encodes.** Operational equity judgment from Equity and Inclusion Operations practice — a governed digital simulation of that practice, not a fake persona chatbot. Staff-facing brand remains **One DHS Support / resource program**. The Mindset Twin is internal, governed, and reviewable operating judgment — never the public product identity and never a substitute for human authority.

**Reject performative equity.** Meet inexperienced staff where they are; graduate capability. Provide a private, low-shame path for introverts and for people uncomfortable asking a person of color in management or DEIA roles — Ask, community intelligence, and knowledge tools first; optional human consult when needed.

| Layer | What it is | What staff see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Ecosystem** | Shared standards, partnership spine, tool portfolio, governance, evaluation | Shared program identity and commitments |
| **Staff Program** | Self-directed Ask, community intelligence, knowledge base, learning, tools, observances, consult handoff | Home, Guided Start, Ask, Learn, Minnesota Communities, Resources, Support / Consult |
| **Practice Workspace** | Protected workflows for authorized practitioners; consultation intake queue for the practice owner | Consultation, analysis, facilitation, work products |
| **Mindset Twin** | Encoded Equity and Inclusion Operations judgment under governance and human review | Not branded as a personal chatbot; appears only as assistive workflows with clear human gates |

**Thesis.** If DHS combines human consultative leadership, a self-directed scale layer, Equity Director stewardship, governed knowledge, accessible learning, practical workflows, partnership infrastructure, and a controlled reasoning layer, the agency can increase the reach and durability of equity practice without flattening local authority, replacing human accountability, or performing equity theater.

**Partnership spine (non-negotiable).** Equity is everyone's work · Build on existing infrastructure · Center lived experience · Follow the data · Move at the speed of trust · Work in partnership.

---

## 2. Problem and opportunity

| Problem | Opportunity for this product |
| --- | --- |
| Equity assets exist but are hard to find and connect at the moment of work | One coherent staff entry point with clear next actions |
| Training alone does not change policies, budgets, forms, contracts, or gates | Practice tools and workflows that produce documented decisions and owners |
| Equity expertise is finite (~180 DSD / ~4,000 agency / ~39 partners) and cannot babysit every launch | Self-directed Ask, community intelligence, and knowledge paths that encode practice judgment; human consult remains available |
| Staff need more than a library or performative training | Orientation, Ask, learning, tools, and a private low-shame path that graduates people toward independent execution |
| Program launches miss equity until too late | Early scoping intake and calendar consult handoff so the practice owner gets heads-up before meetings |
| Leaders need visibility without surveillance | Aggregate, privacy-safe ecosystem views — never personnel ranking |

---

## 3. Product portfolio map (four layers)

| Layer | Purpose | Primary authority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DHS equity infrastructure ecosystem | Purpose, partnership spine, standards, curriculum, access commitments, governance, evaluation, tool portfolio | Program owner with defined DHS governance |
| Staff program | Open learning, communities, observances, resources, tools, multimedia, support | Program owner; approved content owners |
| Equity-practice workspace | Inventory, consultation, analysis, facilitation, planning, work products, follow-up | Authorized practitioners; human decision owners |
| Mindset twin control plane | Stance, reasoning, protected workflows, evaluation, behavior releases, override | Program owner with defined human review |

Administration environments sit under the staff program and practice workspace: Equity Directors steward local pages, priorities, pilots, and contribution within assigned scope. Demonstration and offline modes use synthetic or local data only.

---

## 4. North-star outcomes

| Outcome | What changes | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Staff capability | Staff find, understand, and apply knowledge during real work | Task success, comprehension, later application |
| Capability transfer | Staff graduate from assisted use toward independent equity execution on their own programs | Reduced repeat dependency for comparable work; self-reported confidence; completed self-directed paths before optional consult |
| Access | Language, disability, process, and communication barriers are noticed and addressed earlier | Access testing, remediation closure, user evidence |
| Workplace culture | Supervisors and teams improve climate, participation, candor, and equitable people practices | Practice evidence, climate indicators, qualitative follow-up |
| Institutional application | Equity analysis influences policy, program, budget, technology, procurement, and implementation | Recorded dispositions, changed designs, owners, review dates |
| Organizational memory | Knowledge, decisions, and useful artifacts remain available beyond individual tenure | Governed versions, reuse, review cadence |
| Agency coherence | Administrations work from common standards while preserving local authority | Pilot evidence, adoption, governance decisions |

---

## 5. Boundaries: is / is not

### 5.1 Is

- A self-service / self-directed resource program that scales Equity and Inclusion Operations practice (assist; do not babysit).
- An agencywide professional-development and organizational-change staff layer for a DHS equity infrastructure ecosystem.
- A governed digital learning, Ask, community-intelligence, and knowledge platform with optional human consult handoff.
- A practical equity-work environment for authorized users, including consultation intake for the practice owner.
- A distributed implementation model led by Equity Directors.
- A controlled professional reasoning layer encoding Equity and Inclusion Operations judgment for bounded workflows under human authority — not a personal chatbot identity.

### 5.2 Is not

| Hard boundary | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Not a case system | No eligibility, claims, assessment, personnel, accommodation, complaint, investigation, or records system |
| Not surveillance | No employee ranking, belief profiling, or mandatory ideological-compliance scoring |
| Not icon-only UI | No icons, pictograms, or symbol-only status, completion, or navigation cues in staff-facing work |
| Not single-model dependency | Models, hosting, storage, search, and media services remain replaceable |
| Not a substitute for authority | Does not replace official policy, legal advice, civil-rights processes, Employee Culture, or person-specific decisions |
| Not an autonomous publisher | Does not publish staff-facing material or send official communications without human approval |
| Not performative equity theater | Does not optimize for appearance, checkbox completion, or ideological display; meets staff where they are and measures capability transfer |
| Not a personal chatbot | Does not present as a named persona standing in for a person of color in management/DEIA roles |

---

## 6. Audiences and roles

| Role | Primary value | Authority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DHS staff | Find, learn, practice, use tools, request support | Use staff services; no content-governance authority |
| Supervisors and leaders | Prepare teams, decisions, climate responses, implementation | Use leadership capabilities within job authority |
| Equity Directors and Specialists | Lead pilots, steward local content, improve implementation | Manage assigned administration scope only |
| Program and operational professionals | Apply equity to policy, service design, data, communications, procurement | Create work products; formal decisions stay with responsible officials |
| Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant | Scoping/goals advice on launches; encode practice into self-directed paths; human consults | Practice authority for consult queue and method encoding; product authority shared with program owner |
| Program owner | Coherence, stance, platform, publication, evaluation, adaptive behavior | Final product authority subject to resolved DHS operating agreement |
| Reviewers and maintainers | Content or system review | Least-privilege, time-limited, or technical authority only |

---

## 7. Early-2027 MVP (MUST) vs Pilot-ready vs Deferred

### 7.1 MUST — Early-2027 MVP

| Area | Included |
| --- | --- |
| Staff experience | Coherent Home, Guided Start, Learn, Minnesota Communities, Observances, Equity at Work, Resources, Support |
| **Ask (MUST)** | Self-directed Q&A for policy, practice, intercultural, access, and workplace-culture questions; plain-language answers with uncertainty and human-escalation paths; private/low-shame by design |
| **Community intelligence (MUST)** | Minnesota community knowledge with progressive disclosure; quality criteria met; not artificial sameness |
| Knowledge base / tools | Searchable resources and practical tools that support independent execution, not content tourism |
| Consultation intake / queue | Structured intake so the practice owner gets heads-up before meetings; calendar/consult handoff optional after self-directed attempt |
| Content | Priority content current, owner-reviewed, accessible, representation-reviewed, approved |
| Equity Directors | Pilot package: onboarding, facilitation, evaluation, contribution guidance |
| Governance | Publication, restoration, review workflows tested |
| Scope isolation | Administration contributors work only in assigned scope; denial tests pass |
| Operations | End-user guide, support model, accessibility evidence, security review, recovery rehearsal, deployment revision, rollback target |
| Mindset twin (limited) | Only the three named workflows that pass must-pass gates (Section 11); staff brand remains One DHS Support / resource program |
| Adaptive intelligence baseline | Model/agent definitions exist as product configuration (not hard-coded); upgrade pathway documented; agentic behavior ambitious inside bounded self-service workflows |

### 7.2 Pilot-ready (may ship behind flags; not enterprise claims)

| Area | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| Ecosystem intelligence core | Charter, taxonomy, data model outline, capability domains (no composite score), access zones, privacy rules, stewardship model, limited collection workflow |
| Practice workspace | Limited analysis and facilitation drafts under human approval (intake/queue is MUST in §7.1) |
| Administration pilots | Named administrations only; findings dispositioned before scale claims |

### 7.3 Deferred (Phase 2+)

| Deferred item | Why deferred |
| --- | --- |
| Full ecosystem metric registry and comparative dashboards | Requires approved charter, privacy, Tribal gates, dual-rating |
| Advanced ECO-* analytic claims (causation, network gap inference, resource ratios as performance) | Phase 3+ constraints only (Section 14) |
| Broad autonomous agent expansion beyond the three workflows | Autonomy is earned per workflow |
| Direct DHS system integrations | Separate security, privacy, legal, records, and architecture decision |
| Enterprise representation as an officially authorized DHS system | Ownership/IP/operating agreement gate must clear first |

---

## 8. Staff experience requirements (Phase 1 only)

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| STAFF-01 | Home orients staff to the program and immediate value without internal system language | A new user identifies a useful next action without instruction |
| STAFF-02 | Guided Start recommends a route by need, role, work moment, and desired outcome | Recommendations are optional and explain why they fit |
| STAFF-03 | Search spans learning, communities, resources, observances, tools, support, and approved administration content | Results show content type, authority when applicable, review status, and scope |
| STAFF-04 | Learning supports courses, modules, job aids, scenarios, audio, video, transcripts, optional background notes, and application | Every published learning object meets the common course or resource standard |
| STAFF-05 | Community intelligence uses progressive disclosure without enforcing artificial sameness | Every brief meets common quality criteria; length may vary when evidence requires it |
| STAFF-06 | My Workspace provides continuity for drafts, saved items, progress, requests, and outputs where mode permits | Users understand what is stored, where, and how to delete it |
| STAFF-07 | Support answers broad questions and connects users to consultation when an answer alone is insufficient | Uncertainty, limitations, and human escalation are visible |
| STAFF-08 | Staff-facing copy uses ordinary human language; no model brand names or implementation jargon as product identity | Copy review finds no model names, hidden-system language, or technical labels in staff routes or staff-facing generated responses |
| STAFF-09 | Ask answers policy, practice, intercultural, access, and workplace-culture questions with sources/limits visible | Moderated tasks show useful answer or clear escalate-to-human path without requiring a person-of-color gatekeeper |
| STAFF-10 | Consultation intake captures program stage, goals, equity questions, and desired outcome before calendar handoff | Practice owner receives structured heads-up; staff can complete intake without a live meeting |
| STAFF-11 | Self-directed paths cue independent next actions before optional consult | Users can complete a comparable task path without defaulting to "book a meeting" |

### 8.1 Self-directed resource paths

The staff program scales Equity and Inclusion Operations practice through four complementary paths. Face-to-face and calendar consults remain available; the application assists and does not replace them.

| Path | Staff value | Product rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Ask** | Private, low-shame questions on policy, practice, intercultural competence, access, and workplace culture | Early-2027 MUST. Answer with governed knowledge; show uncertainty; never invent authority; escalate when human judgment is required |
| **Community intelligence** | Minnesota community knowledge usable at the moment of work | Early-2027 MUST. Progressive disclosure; quality over sameness; lived-experience and partnership spine respected |
| **Knowledge base / resources / tools** | Seeds and fertilizer for independent execution | Prefer actionable tools and job aids over passive content consumption; measure application, not clicks alone |
| **Optional human consult** | Calendar / queue handoff when self-directed paths are insufficient | Structured intake first (program stage, goals, equity embed questions, desired outcome) so the practice owner is prepared; assist, do not babysit |

**Graduation stance.** Meet inexperienced staff where they are. Reject performative checkbox equity. Success is staff who can embed equity considerations in their own launches with less repeated dependency on the same human consultant for comparable work.

---

## 9. Equity Director pilot model (compact)

Equity Directors lead administration pilots. Pilots do not decide whether the agencywide program exists; they decide how the shared program is contextualized, supported, improved, and scaled.

| Responsibility | Program owner provides | Equity Director leads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Readiness | Standards, platform, content baseline, accessibility evidence, pilot package | Local sponsor alignment, participant scope, risks, readiness |
| Implementation | Pathways, facilitation tools, support, technical operations | Local sequencing, communication, facilitation, adaptation within boundaries |
| Evaluation | Common measures, instruments, privacy rules, analysis support | Context interpretation, participant protection, local learning, recommendations |
| Scale decision | Cross-pilot synthesis, remediation plan, agencywide options | Administration disposition and conditions for expansion |

**Pilot decision standard.** Staff can find trusted support faster, understand how to use it, apply it to real work, and identify when human authority is required. The pilot also produces actionable evidence about inaccessible, outdated, missing, confusing, or difficult-to-apply elements.

---

## 10. Adaptive Program Intelligence (product expectations)

The program is an adaptive platform: the intelligence layer can improve as models and tools improve, without rebuilding the application. It must evolve continuously but not drift casually. Agentic behavior should be ambitious inside bounded self-service workflows (Ask, triage, classification, accessibility review, consult prep) — not timid content search only — while remaining within tool boundaries and human gates.

| Expectation | Product meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Model evolution | Approved models are registered with purpose, scope, cost/risk notes, and which agents may use them. Switching models does not require rewriting staff routes |
| Agent definitions | Each agent has purpose, allowed inputs/outputs, scope, review rule, evaluation test, and enabled/disabled state |
| Evaluations | New models are judged on program tasks: accuracy, scope adherence, plain language, accessibility checks, no surveillance behavior, human-gate respect — not on impressiveness |
| Upgrade pathway | Candidate → evaluation cases → compare → sandbox → limited pilot → owner review → enable / hold / reject |
| Durable program memory | Preserve approved decisions, review outcomes, content history, scope rules, published versions, accepted/rejected recommendations, evaluation results — not loose chat residue |
| Tool boundaries | Agents may draft, classify, check accessibility, prepare agendas, summarize de-identified themes. Agents may not publish, send official messages, make HR/legal decisions, handle complaints, act on case data, rank staff, or change another administration's content |

Detail for adapters, prompt versioning, feature flags, and eval harness belongs in the TRD.

---

## 11. Mindset twin — product role, first three workflows, autonomy rules

### 11.1 Product role

The mindset twin is a protected operating reasoning layer: the **encoded operating judgment of the Equity and Inclusion Operations practice** (the principal architect's method), governed and reviewable. It is a digital simulation of that practice under governance — **not** a fake persona chatbot, **not** a named substitute for a person of color in management/DEIA roles, and **not** the public identity of the staff program. Staff-facing brand remains One DHS Support / resource program.

It helps authorized users sense, analyze, design, plan, prepare, review, evaluate, and improve bounded work under human authority. Stance: systems-oriented, people-focused, humble, discreet, evidence-humble, anti-performative, and able to work through bureaucracy without being captured by it.

### 11.2 First three workflows (must-pass intent)

| Workflow | Must-pass intent | Autonomy ceiling at launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **(a) Resource classification** | Correctly classify resource type, audience, authority status, currency, and review need; surface uncertainty; never invent authority | A2 Produce drafts; human confirms classification before publication impact |
| **(b) Plain-language and accessibility review** | Flag unclear language, missing structure, contrast/alt/caption risks, and inaccessible interaction patterns; propose remediations; never claim WCAG pass without evidence | A2 Produce review drafts; human owns release disposition |
| **(c) Consultation triage / agenda prep** | First-class intake/queue: structured questions (program stage, goals, equity embed asks, desired outcome) so the practice owner gets heads-up before meetings; propose agenda with owners and timeboxes; escalate when human judgment is required; never decide the consultation outcome | A2 Produce agenda/intake drafts; A3 only for reversible routing/scheduling with undo |

### 11.3 Autonomy ladder (earned)

| Level | Agent authority | Required control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A0 Observe | Read, classify, summarize, detect patterns | Visible activity; no external action |
| A1 Recommend | Propose questions, options, learning, next steps | Designated human chooses |
| A2 Produce | Create complete editable drafts and artifacts | Human edit / approve / reject / regenerate |
| A3 Execute reversible | Save, organize, route, schedule, update state, run checks | Undo, pause, limits, activity history |
| A4 Run bounded workflow | Complete a predefined multi-step process within limits | Approval gates, exception review, rollback |
| A5 Propose adaptation | Candidate behavior or content improvements from evidence | Only program owner promotes to production |

Autonomy percentages are aspirations, not release requirements. Success is safe, useful completion and appropriate escalation.

---

## 12. Content and accessibility standards (compact)

| Standard | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Accessibility target | WCAG 2.2 AA and applicable Section 508 expectations across staff, contributor, owner, and generated artifacts |
| No-icons rule | Staff-facing interfaces contain no icon, pictogram, or symbol-only control, progress, or navigation indicators |
| Canonical content | One content object governs all renditions (web, Word, PDF, slides, audio, video) with ID, version, owner, authority status, review date, language, accessibility status |
| Owner admissibility | System may surface missing context; only the designated human owner publishes, qualifies, revises, holds, or rejects |
| Migration rule | Existing One DSD artifacts are migration inputs, not automatic approval, authority, or accessibility proof. Preserve useful substance; require explicit human disposition. Missing context never auto-removes an item |
| Representation | Medium alone (including AI-assisted imagery) does not decide approval. Purpose, rights, realism, context, accessibility, representational risk, and owner decision govern. Photorealistic synthetic imagery must not be presented as documentary evidence of a real person, event, or community |
| Interactive learning | Keyboard and assistive-technology paths required; drag tasks need non-drag alternatives |
| Generated artifacts | Word, PDF, PowerPoint, Excel, audio, video must meet accessibility requirements before publication or formal delivery |

---

## 13. Privacy, security, environment separation (compact)

| Control | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Prohibited PII in staff learning | No case, eligibility, service-authorization, medical, disability, personnel, complaint, investigation, SSN, or comparable PII required or retained in staff learning |
| Environment separation | Mindset-private, pilot, administration, demonstration, and future enterprise data remain technically and operationally separated |
| Auth and privilege | Protected workspaces require strong authentication, exact authorization, least privilege |
| Logging | Privacy-safe logs; no prohibited payloads in review links or exports |
| External services | Minimum approved data only; retention and regional processing documented before use with protected work |
| Completion data | Approved purpose, notice, minimum fields, retention/deletion, correction; **prohibited** for employee ranking or discipline |
| Portable exports | No live telemetry endpoints that transmit names, email, teams, activity, or completion outside the approved authenticated environment |
| DHS system integration | Out of initial release; requires separate security, privacy, legal, records, architecture, and authority decision |

---

## 14. Ecosystem intelligence — product constraints for later phases

MVP may provide a structured asset inventory, audited resource measures, domain capability profiles, and descriptive network maps under pilot-ready rules (Section 7.2).

**Refused always (including Phase 3+):**

- Composite maturity / enterprise scores
- Fake causal ratios (including disparities-addressed ÷ disparities-identified)
- Personnel ranking or performance scorecards from ecosystem data
- Public leaderboards of administrations or programs
- Automated funding or program decisions
- Gap/duplication flags from network degree alone
- Tribal affiliation inference; Nation-governed data without documented authority

**Phase 3+ constraints (summary — full ECO-* registry lives in Operating Model / TRD / Knowledge Map, not this PRD):**

| Constraint family | Product rule |
| --- | --- |
| Evidence labeling | Descriptive, associative, contribution, and causal claims stay distinct; unsupported causal language blocked in publication |
| Capability domains | Separate evidence-based domains; dual-rating and agreement thresholds before comparative release |
| Resources | Direct / embedded / shared / pass-through / contracted stay distinct; ratios never become performance proxies alone |
| Network | Typed, temporal edges; corroboration required before gap or duplication findings |
| Privacy / Tribal | Field-level authority before ingestion; Tribal features disabled until consultation and agreements exist |
| Human disposition | Every consequential finding links to investigate / connect / support / sustain / redesign / scale / discontinue with owner and review date |

---

## 15. Launch success metrics and release gates

### 15.1 Exact launch KPIs (any fail blocks release)

| KPI ID | Metric | Fail threshold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| KPI-01 | New-user task success on Home → useful next action | < 80% of moderated test participants succeed without instruction |
| KPI-02 | Search finds a relevant approved item for five scripted staff tasks | < 4 of 5 tasks succeed |
| KPI-03 | Priority published content accessibility | Any unresolved release-blocking WCAG 2.2 AA barrier in representative staff journeys |
| KPI-04 | No-icons / plain-language staff copy gate | Any icon-only cue or model-brand product identity in staff routes |
| KPI-05 | Administration scope isolation | Any successful cross-administration write in denial tests |
| KPI-06 | Prohibited PII controls | Any staff-learning path that requires or retains prohibited PII in test cases |
| KPI-07 | Mindset workflows must-pass suite | Any failure on must-pass cases for workflows (a)–(c) |
| KPI-08 | Rollback readiness | No named rollback target or failed recovery rehearsal |
| KPI-09 | Ownership decision gate | Enterprise representation attempted without written ownership/operating agreement |
| KPI-10 | Browser-flow release gate | Critical staff, editor, Program Steward, review, publishing, and administration journeys not exercised in the running application |
| KPI-11 | Capability transfer (independence) | Moderated cohort shows no measurable path from Ask/resources to independent next action; or consult intake is the only offered route for routine questions |
| KPI-12 | Ask + Community Intelligence MUST presence | Ask or Minnesota community intelligence missing, non-functional, or gated only behind live consult in Early-2027 MVP build |

### 15.2 Release gates

| Gate | Pass condition |
| --- | --- |
| Product | Purpose, staff value, roles, scope, and pilot-to-scale model approved |
| Ownership | Stewardship, DHS use, branding, portability, data, derivative work, and continuity resolved **in writing** before enterprise representation |
| Content | Published items meet authority, currency, owner decision, representation, and lifecycle standards |
| Accessibility | No unresolved release-blocking barriers in representative workflows |
| Security / privacy | Environment separation, authorization, secrets, uploads, logging, recovery, prohibited-data controls pass |
| Mindset quality | Included workflows pass fidelity, evidence, authority, harmful-output, escalation, and rollback evaluations |
| Operations | Named owners, capacity, support, incident response, administration onboarding, deployment evidence, rollback exist |
| Ecosystem (if pilot-ready ships) | Charter, prohibited uses, taxonomy outline, access zones, privacy rules, Tribal gates, stewardship approved — still no composite scores |

---

## 16. Decision log (unresolved gates)

| ID | Decision | Owner | Due | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D-01 | Confirm official portfolio naming: Ecosystem / Staff Program / Practice Workspace / Mindset Twin | Program owner | TBD | Open |
| D-02 | Resolve agencywide DHS operating model and IP/stewardship questions for the protected mindset layer | Program owner + DHS sponsors / legal as assigned | TBD | Open — hard gate |
| D-03 | Freeze Early-2027 MVP vs deferred list (this PRD §7) | Program owner | TBD | Proposed — needs owner sign-off |
| D-04 | Name Equity Director pilot governance group, participating administrations, decision process | Program owner + Equity Directors | TBD | Open |
| D-05 | Approve Ecosystem charter, prohibited uses, taxonomy, access zones, privacy, Tribal gates, stewardship for pilot-ready scope | Program owner + data / privacy / Tribal partners as assigned | TBD | Open — hard gate for comparative analytics |
| D-06 | Approve representation and visual-content standard (including responsible AI-assisted imagery) | Program owner | TBD | Open |
| D-07 | Assign authority status, owners, remediation, and migration disposition for existing One DSD / One DHS artifacts | Program owner + content owners | TBD | Open |
| D-08 | Approve authentication, data separation, hosting, records, privacy, and security boundaries per environment | Program owner + security / privacy as assigned | TBD | Open |
| D-09 | Confirm first three mindset workflows and must-pass evaluation cases (this PRD §11) | Program owner | TBD | Proposed — needs owner sign-off |
| D-10 | Name accountable owners and capacity for content, accessibility, technology, support, evaluation, incident response | Program owner | TBD | Open |
| D-11 | Canonical source freeze before build expansion (Appendix A) | Program owner + engineering lead | TBD | Open — hard gate for expansion |
| D-12 | Tribal / enterprise representation and branding permissions for any official DHS claim | Program owner + appropriate DHS / Tribal authorities | TBD | Open — hard gate |

Ownership, IP, Tribal, and enterprise representation remain **hard gates**. This PRD does not imply they are resolved.

---

## 17. Risks and mitigations (top 8)

| # | Risk | Consequence | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Application mistaken for the whole program or for babysitting | Change collapses into content consumption or performative checkboxes | Fund facilitation and human consult; measure capability transfer; assist, do not replace judgment |
| 2 | Mindset twin eclipses staff purpose or appears as a personal chatbot | Trust declines; product appears as an AI persona standing in for DEIA staff | Keep twin in protected architecture; staff brand is One DHS Support / resource program; lead with self-directed paths and human consult |
| 3 | Ownership / DHS authority remain ambiguous | Adoption, continuity, branding, and investment unstable | Written agreement before enterprise representation (D-02, D-12) |
| 4 | Autonomy target drives unsafe expansion | Activity optimized over judgment | Authorize autonomy by workflow, consequence, evidence, reversibility |
| 5 | Comprehensive becomes ungovernable | Content sprawl, stale guidance, overload | Progressive disclosure, lifecycle, retirement, evidence-based prioritization |
| 6 | Ecosystem inventory becomes leaderboard or surveillance | Units hide problems; trust collapses | Prohibit composite rankings and personnel use; challenge rights; human dispositions |
| 7 | Source sprawl / wrong tree built | Lost work or building from non-canonical code | Canonical source freeze (Appendix A) before expansion |
| 8 | Tribal relationships reduced to demographic records | Sovereignty and trust harmed | Nation-specific governance; features off until authority documented |

---

## 18. Definition of done for Phase 1

Phase 1 is done when **all** of the following are true:

1. Sections 7.1 MUST items are implemented and demonstrated in the running application.
2. STAFF-01 through STAFF-11 acceptance criteria pass moderated review.
3. KPI-01 through KPI-12 either pass or have an explicit owner-approved exception with remediation date (exceptions cannot waive Ownership or prohibited-PII gates).
4. Mindset workflows (a)–(c) pass must-pass suites; no other protected intelligent workflows are enabled in production.
5. Accessibility, security/privacy, and operations release gates pass.
6. Decision log items D-02, D-11, and D-12 are either closed or explicitly blocked from enterprise claims.
7. Migration dispositions exist for priority One DSD / One DHS artifacts included in launch content.
8. Rollback target is named and recovery rehearsal succeeded.

The program is not “done” because every future feature exists. It is ready to scale when people can do better work, authority remains human and explicit, and improvement compounds through evidence rather than drift.

---

## Appendix A. Source-of-truth and migration posture

**Current uncertainty (as of September 4, 2026 inventory):**

| Finding | Implication |
| --- | --- |
| Multiple local trees and large generated folders exist | High risk of building from the wrong root |
| GitHub `one-dhs-equity-resource` is the strongest recoverable One DHS source (linked Git + Vercel project) | Prefer this line for One DHS application continuity pending freeze |
| One DSD live provenance is unresolved relative to known rebuild sources | Do not treat any single local tree as proven live provenance without verification |
| Uncommitted changes exist in recoverable repos | Freeze before cleanup or expansion |
| Advanced production trees contain unique source/media amid generated material | Retain unique assets; do not bulk-delete without comparison |

**PRD requirement.** Canonical source freeze is a hard gate before build expansion:

1. Name the canonical application repository and branch for One DHS PAC.
2. Record live deployment mapping (project ↔ commit ↔ URL).
3. Inventory uncommitted work and either commit, stash with owner approval, or discard with written disposition.
4. Separate migration inputs (One DSD artifacts, media, governed content) from build caches and disposable generated output.
5. Only after freeze: expand build work and staged cleanup of non-canonical material.

**Migration rule (repeat).** Useful substance may migrate; an existing file does not decide approval, authority, accessibility, or currency.

---

## Appendix B. Mapping from prior PRD versions (what moved where)

**v2.0 → v2.1 (owner framing, September 4, 2026).** §1 rewritten to lead with human consultative role + self-directed scale layer; §8.1 Self-directed resource paths (Ask, community intelligence, knowledge base, optional consult) added; Ask and Community Intelligence locked into Early-2027 MUST; consultation intake/queue made first-class; capability-transfer outcomes and KPIs added; Mindset Twin clarified as encoded Equity and Inclusion Operations judgment (not a personal chatbot); Adaptive Program Intelligence gains ambitious-but-bounded agentic expectation. Structure otherwise unchanged from v2.0.

| v1.2 area | v2.x treatment |
| --- | --- |
| §1 Executive product definition | §1 One-page product definition; four-layer split; v2.1 human+scale framing |
| §2 Problem / partnership spine / domains / leverage | §2 tight problem table; spine kept; domain/leverage detail → Operating Model / Knowledge Map |
| §3 North-star outcomes | §4 retained; v2.1 adds capability transfer |
| §4 Program architecture | §3 Product portfolio map |
| §5 Boundaries | §5 retained and sharpened; v2.1 anti-performative / not-persona rows |
| §6 Audiences | §6 retained; v2.1 adds Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant |
| §7 Agencywide components / practice principles | Summarized into §1–§4; full principle tables → Operating Model |
| §8 Staff experience | §8 Phase 1 + §8.1 self-directed paths (v2.1) |
| §9 Equity Director pilot | §9 compact |
| §10 Equity-practice workflows | Deferred detail → Practice Workspace backlog; consultation intake in §7.1 / §8.1 / §11 |
| §11–§13 Mindset twin / autonomy / MIND-* | §11 + autonomy ladder; encoded practice judgment clarified in v2.1; MIND detail → TRD / eval suites |
| §14–§15 Content / representation | §12 compact; CNT/EDIT/HR IDs → Knowledge Map / TRD |
| §16–§17 Governance / ownership gate | §15–§16; ownership softened as unresolved hard gate |
| §18 Accessibility | §12 |
| §19 Privacy / security | §13 |
| §20 Ecosystem intelligence + full ECO-* registry | §14 constraints only; registry not pasted |
| §21–§23 Measurement / NFR / delivery phases | §15 KPIs (incl. v2.1 transfer / Ask MUST); NFR → TRD; phases compressed into §7 |
| §24–§25 Launch minimum / release gates | §7 + §15 |
| §26 Risks | §17 top 8 |
| §27 Decisions required | §16 Decision log with Owner / Due / Status |
| §28–§29 Success / input reconciliation | §18 + Appendix B |
| Adaptive Program Intelligence (post-v1.2 direction) | §10; v2.1 ambitious-within-bounds sentence |
| Source inventory findings | Appendix A |

---

*Internal planning document · One DHS People, Access and Culture · Product PRD v2.1 · September 4, 2026*

# One DHS PAC Product PRD — v2.1 change summary

**For:** parent agent / planning handoff  
**Date:** September 4, 2026 (America/Chicago)  
**Files:**
- `/workspace/One-DHS-People-Access-and-Culture-Product-PRD-v2.md` (source of truth)
- `/workspace/One-DHS-People-Access-and-Culture-Product-PRD-v2.docx` (regenerated)

## What changed (v2.0 → v2.1)

Owner framing from Gary Banks (Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant / principal architect) is now encoded without expanding back into a mega-doc (~435 → ~472 lines).

1. **§1 rewritten** to lead with human consultative role (scoping/goals on launches) **plus** a self-directed scale layer (~180 DSD / ~4,000 agency / ~39 partners). Application assists; does not replace face-to-face/calendar consults; graduates staff toward independent equity execution (seeds/fertilizer; they water the garden).
2. **§8.1 Self-directed resource paths** added: Ask, Community intelligence, Knowledge base/tools, Optional human consult with structured intake.
3. **Early-2027 MUST** now explicitly includes **Ask** and **Community Intelligence**, plus consultation intake/queue and knowledge/tools for independent execution.
4. **Capability transfer / independence** added as north-star outcome, STAFF-09–11, and KPI-11/KPI-12 (not content consumption alone).
5. **Mindset Twin** clarified as encoded operating judgment of Equity and Inclusion Operations practice — governed/reviewable digital simulation of method — **not** a personal chatbot identity. Staff brand remains One DHS Support / resource program.
6. **Consultation intake/queue** is first-class (structured heads-up before meetings) across §7.1, §8.1, STAFF-10, and workflow (c).
7. **Adaptive Program Intelligence:** one sentence requiring ambitious agentic behavior inside bounded self-service workflows (not timid search-only).
8. **Anti-performative** and hard safety boundaries retained/strengthened (no surveillance, no case data, not persona, not checkbox theater).
9. **Appendix B** updated with v2.0→v2.1 mapping note.
10. **Version 2.1** · Status: *Proposed product baseline reflecting owner framing*.

## Recommended next 5 build/planning steps

1. **Freeze Ask + Community Intelligence MVP contracts** — intents, knowledge sources, uncertainty/escalation UX, progressive-disclosure rules; write must-pass eval cases before UI polish.
2. **Design consultation intake schema + queue** — fields for program stage, goals, equity-embed questions, desired outcome; calendar handoff; practice-owner heads-up view (workflow (c) must-pass).
3. **Map self-directed graduation paths** — for 3–5 common launch types, define Ask → resources/tools → optional consult sequences; instrument KPI-11 independence evidence.
4. **Canonical source freeze (Appendix A / D-11)** — name repo/branch and live deploy mapping before expanding build work on Ask/CI features.
5. **Staff copy / brand pass** — enforce One DHS Support / resource program language; strip any personal-chatbot or model-brand identity from routes; align Home/Guided Start with §8.1 paths.

## Non-goals this revision did not reopen

Operating Model internals, full ECO-* registry, TRD schemas, ownership/IP hard gates (D-02/D-12), Tribal consultation records.

# One DHS Support — Reference Harvest Brief

**For:** Gary Banks  
**Date:** September 4, 2026  
**Status:** Collaborative working brief (decision confirmed)  
**Sources (live):**  
- Color: [one-dhs-equity-resource.vercel.app](https://one-dhs-equity-resource.vercel.app/)  
- Structure/content patterns: that app **and** [one-dsd-resource-hub-live.vercel.app](https://one-dsd-resource-hub-live.vercel.app/)  
**Assets on box:** `/workspace/live-ref/dhs-equity/` (`dhs-logo.png`, `staff-hero-office.jpg`)

---

## 1. Confirmed decision

| Item | Decision |
|------|----------|
| Color | Pull from **One DHS Equity Resource** (canonical brand) |
| Structure / content patterns | Harvest useful IA and UX patterns from **both** live apps |
| Architecture | **Do not** clone either app’s architecture |
| Product direction | Self-directed resource program + **agentic scale layer** from PRD v2.1 pack: Ask, Community Intelligence, consult intake, graduation paths, Adaptive Program Intelligence |
| Brand | Staff-facing **One DHS Support** |
| Deploy | GitHub + Vercel from **Gary’s PC** (not Origin) |

Harvest = tokens + proven patterns. Build = new product on PRD v2.1, not a fork.

---

## 2. Color & type tokens (canonical — One DHS)

| Role | Token | Notes |
|------|--------|--------|
| Navy (primary) | `#003865` / `#00365f` | Core brand navy (both appear live) |
| Deep navy | `#024` / `#002342` | Headers, depth, dark surfaces |
| Mid navy | `#004f90` | Links / mid accents |
| Green (primary accent) | `#78be21` | Primary CTA / accent |
| Green (rare) | `#3c6b1f` | Occasional; **not** primary for One DHS Support |
| Font stack | Aptos, Aptos Display, Segoe UI, Calibri, system-ui | Prefer Aptos → system fallbacks |
| Hero image | `/images/staff-hero-office.jpg` | Saved: `live-ref/dhs-equity/staff-hero-office.jpg` |
| Logo | `/images/dhs-logo.png` | Saved: `live-ref/dhs-equity/dhs-logo.png` |

**Contrast only (One DSD — not primary brand):** navy `#00365f`, navy-dark `#002342`, green `#3c6b1f` / `#2f7a14`. Use for pattern comparison; do not adopt as One DHS Support palette.

---

## 3. Harvest from One DHS (keep / adapt / leave)

| Pattern | Keep | Adapt | Leave |
|---------|------|-------|-------|
| Foundation / Learn / Apply / Lead (“Four Doors”) | Strong mental model | Or fold into Guided Start + graduation paths (open Q) | Don’t ship as the only nav forever |
| Equity in Practice (6 perspectives + 7 questions) | Core reflection content | Slim for agencywide staff; agent-assisted prompts | Don’t paste as a static mega-page only |
| Equity at Work | Workplace application framing | Tie to role / division context | Standalone silo |
| Ask / support | Entry for help | Wire to **Ask** + consult intake (PRD) | Old “content FAQ only” Ask |
| Communities | Peer / community signal | Feed **Community Intelligence** | Social clone without governance |
| Resource library | Browse / search habit | Tag to graduation paths + program intelligence | Dump-all library with no paths |
| Calendar / courses / learning | Cadence & learning objects | Align to Adaptive Program Intelligence | Course LMS rebuild |
| Orientation–culture, professional support | Onboarding & growth | Map to graduation paths | Parallel orphan sections |
| Map / start | Wayfinding | Prefer Guided Start if Four Doors softens | Duplicate start experiences |
| Audio briefing on equity | Accessible modality | Optional, agent-summarizable | Mandatory media dependency |

---

## 4. Harvest from One DSD (keep / adapt / leave)

| Pattern | Keep | Adapt | Leave |
|---------|------|-------|-------|
| Division-centered work areas (waivers, CFSS, MnCHOICES, etc.) | Clarity of “where I work” | Light agencywide slices—not full DSD hub depth (open Q) | Rebuilding every DSD work area 1:1 |
| Role-based audiences | Staff self-location | Map roles → paths / Ask routing | Hard-coded audience silos |
| Safety boundaries (no client info, Tribal paths, private reflection) | **Must keep** as product rules | Surface in Ask, intake, CI, copy | Soft / buried disclaimers only |
| Resource browse + calendar | Proven discovery | Shared patterns under One DHS Support IA | Second competing hub UI |
| Minnesota Communities / cultural observance calendar | Community & cultural rhythm | Optional modules; CI-aware | Primary brand green / DSD chrome |

---

## 5. Explicitly NOT rebuilding

- Neither live app’s **architecture** (routing, data model, component tree, deploy story as-is).
- A **shallow content-only** resource site (pages without Ask, CI, intake, graduation, Adaptive Program Intelligence).
- **Origin**-based cloud deploy path — ship **GitHub + Vercel from Gary’s PC**.
- One DSD as **primary brand** (palette or “division hub” as the whole product).
- Clone of Four Doors / Equity IA as a frozen shell with no agentic layer.
- Client-data workflows or anything that weakens DSD-proven **safety boundaries**.

---

## 6. Open questions for Gary (collaborative)

1. **Entry model:** Keep **Four Doors** (Foundation / Learn / Apply / Lead) as primary IA, or lead with **Guided Start + graduation paths** and treat doors as secondary labels?
2. **Equity in Practice depth:** Carry full 6 perspectives + 7 questions in v1, a slim “practice pack,” or agent-first (Ask surfaces practice on demand)?
3. **DSD work-area depth:** In the agencywide app, how deep should division work areas go—links/outlines only, curated agencywide slices, or selected deep modules (e.g. MnCHOICES)?
4. **Communities vs Community Intelligence:** Is live “communities” primarily a **browse/join** surface, a **signal feed into CI**, or both from day one?
5. **Calendar scope:** One shared staff calendar (learning + cultural observance + events), or separate learning vs cultural tracks with a unified “What’s next” strip?

---

*Brief for collaborative reference harvest — One DHS Support · PRD v2.1 direction · color from One DHS · patterns from both live apps · no architecture clone.*
