## 14. Ecosystem intelligence — product constraints for later phases

MVP may provide a structured asset inventory, audited resource measures, domain capability profiles, and descriptive network maps under pilot-ready rules (Section 7.2).

**Refused always (including Phase 3+):**

- Composite maturity / enterprise scores
- Fake causal ratios (including disparities-addressed ÷ disparities-identified)
- Personnel ranking or performance scorecards from ecosystem data
- Public leaderboards of administrations or programs
- Automated funding or program decisions
- Gap/duplication flags from network degree alone
- Tribal affiliation inference; Nation-governed data without documented authority

**Phase 3+ constraints (summary — full ECO-* registry lives in Operating Model / TRD / Knowledge Map, not this PRD):**

| Constraint family | Product rule |
| --- | --- |
| Evidence labeling | Descriptive, associative, contribution, and causal claims stay distinct; unsupported causal language blocked in publication |
| Capability domains | Separate evidence-based domains; dual-rating and agreement thresholds before comparative release |
| Resources | Direct / embedded / shared / pass-through / contracted stay distinct; ratios never become performance proxies alone |
| Network | Typed, temporal edges; corroboration required before gap or duplication findings |
| Privacy / Tribal | Field-level authority before ingestion; Tribal features disabled until consultation and agreements exist |
| Human disposition | Every consequential finding links to investigate / connect / support / sustain / redesign / scale / discontinue with owner and review date |

## 18. Definition of done for Phase 1

Phase 1 is done when **all** of the following are true:

1. Sections 7.1 MUST items are implemented and demonstrated in the running application.
2. STAFF-01 through STAFF-11 acceptance criteria pass moderated review.
3. KPI-01 through KPI-12 either pass or have an explicit owner-approved exception with remediation date (exceptions cannot waive Ownership or prohibited-PII gates).
4. Mindset workflows (a)–(c) pass must-pass suites; no other protected intelligent workflows are enabled in production.
5. Accessibility, security/privacy, and operations release gates pass.
6. Decision log items D-02, D-11, and D-12 are either closed or explicitly blocked from enterprise claims.
7. Migration dispositions exist for priority One DSD / One DHS artifacts included in launch content.
8. Rollback target is named and recovery rehearsal succeeded.

The program is not “done” because every future feature exists. It is ready to scale when people can do better work, authority remains human and explicit, and improvement compounds through evidence rather than drift.

# One DHS Staff Copy & Brand Pass

**Freezes staff-facing language for One DHS People, Access and Culture**

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Version | 0.1 |
| Date | September 4, 2026 |
| Status | Proposed — copy freeze for Early-2027 MVP |
| Parent | Product PRD v2.1 (STAFF-08, KPI-04) |
| Companions | Ask / CI / Consultation Intake / Graduation Paths contracts; TRD (internal terms only) |
| Audience | Product, design, engineering, content owners, PR reviewers |

---

## 1. Brand identity

**Staff brand:** One DHS Support — a self-directed **resource program** for People, Access and Culture.

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Call it **One DHS Support**, **resource program**, or route names (Ask, Minnesota Communities, Resources, Support) | Call it Gary's tool, Gary's chatbot, or any personal brand |
| Say the program **assists** and helps staff graduate to independent work | Say it babysits, coaches you like a therapist, or replaces human judgment |
| Keep optional **Request a consultation** for calendar / face-to-face handoff | Present consult as the default first step for routine questions |
| Use plain public-service English | Use model brand names, vendor names, or implementation jargon as product identity |
| Text labels for every control, status, and nav item | Icons, pictograms, or symbol-only cues in staff UI |
| Frame as private / low-shame practice support | Frame as surveillance, scoring, ranking, or performative "equity theater" |
| Attribute answers to **approved guidance / Official / Practice note** | Attribute answers to "the AI," a named persona, or the Mindset Twin |

**Internal vs staff:** Mindset Twin, agents, orchestrator, model registry, embeddings, prompts, and autonomy levels are **engineering / Practice Workspace** language. They must **never** appear in staff routes or staff-facing generated copy.

---

## 2. Voice & tone principles

1. **Graduate, don't babysit** — Meet staff where they are; cue independent next actions before optional consult.
2. **Practical** — Prefer tools, checklists, and "what to do next" over abstract theory or content tourism.
3. **Non-shaming** — Inexperienced staff are welcome. Correct gently; never mock or moralize.
4. **Non-theatrical** — No cheerleading, no virtue performance, no checkbox celebration as success.
5. **Private / low-shame** — Ask and resources first; no requirement to ask a person of color in management/DEIA roles for a first answer.
6. **Human authority stays human** — Uncertainty visible; Official status never attaches to generated prose alone.
7. **Anti-stereotype** — Firm on limits without scolding; center partnership and within-group diversity.
8. **Concise public-service English** — Short sentences; expand on demand (progressive disclosure).

---

## 3. Banned words / phrases (staff routes)

| Banned (staff UI / staff-facing generated copy) | Approved alternative |
| --- | --- |
| AI, artificial intelligence, LLM, GPT, Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Copilot, or any model/vendor brand | Omit, or: "this program," "One DHS Support," "guided answers from approved resources" |
| Agent, multi-agent, orchestrator, dispatcher, specialist agent | "Support," "guided help," route name (Ask, Resources) |
| Mindset Twin, twin, persona chatbot, "talk as [named person]" | One DHS Support; refuse persona requests |
| Prompt, system prompt, embedding, vector, RAG, inference, token, temperature | Never staff-visible; say "search," "approved sources," "answer" |
| Model, model registry, provider, adapter, autonomy level (A0–A5) | Internal only; staff see outcomes, not machinery |
| Hallucination (as product copy) | "We don't have an approved source for that" / "This is uncertain" |
| Chatbot, bot, AI assistant, digital twin | Ask / Support / resource program |
| Gary / practice owner's name as product identity | Practice owner may appear only in consult context as a **human** role, not the product name |
| Score, rank, maturity score, equity scorecard (of people/units) | Refuse; offer tools and learning instead |
| "Book a meeting" as sole CTA for routine questions | "Next step" tools first; "Request a consultation" optional |
| Icon-only status ("✓" alone, pictogram nav) | Text: Received, Under review, Completed, etc. |

**Practice Workspace / internal docs** may use TRD terms. Staff Home, Guided Start, Ask, CI, Resources, Support, Graduation/self-check, errors, and empty states may not.

---

## 4. Preferred glossary

| Staff term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **One DHS Support** | Staff-facing brand for the PAC resource program |
| **Ask** | Private Q&A from approved guidance; not a personal chatbot |
| **Minnesota Communities** | Staff name for Community Intelligence briefs |
| **Community Intelligence** | Internal/product name; prefer **Minnesota Communities** in UI chrome |
| **Resources** | Searchable job aids, tools, Learn objects — actionable over tourism |
| **Learn** | Courses, modules, scenarios, job aids |
| **Guided Start** | Optional route-by-need recommender |
| **Support** | Help hub: Ask, Resources, Request a consultation, Track request |
| **Request a consultation** | Structured intake → practice-owner heads-up; calendar optional |
| **Track request** | Status by reference ID (own requests only) |
| **Official / Guidance / Practice note / Learning / Community brief / Under review / External — verify** | Authority labels on answers and content |
| **Self-check** | Anti-performative rubric before marking practice complete |
| **Practice artifact** | Staff-owned checklist, plan, or map for their work |
| **Equity Director** | Local pilot steward (administration scope) — not the product brand |

---

## 5. Route-by-route copy checklist

| Route | Must say / show | Must not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Home** | Program purpose in plain words; 2–4 useful next actions (Ask, Guided Start, Minnesota Communities, Resources, Support) | Internal system language; model/agent terms; icon-only tiles |
| **Guided Start** | Optional recommendations with brief "why this fits"; user chooses | Forced path; consult as only option; ranking language |
| **Ask** | Privacy notice at entry; short answer first; authority labels; uncertainty; independent next actions; "Prepare a consult request" when needed | Persona; invented Official policy; PII processing; "book a meeting" as only CTA |
| **Minnesota Communities (CI)** | Practice support for Minnesota work; Level-0/1 progressive disclosure; work panel: What to ask · Access checks · Who to involve · What not to assume | Encyclopedia / "people types"; profiling individuals; fabricated community facts; Tribal Nation guidance without authority |
| **Resources / Learn** | Actionable tools and job aids; authority/currency cues | Content tourism as success; model brands on generated artifacts |
| **Consult intake** | Privacy + prohibited-data warning; field help in ordinary English; preview of what practice owner sees; share confirmation; graduation cue (try Ask/Resources when routine) | Auto-book meeting; persona; case/PII fields; staff ranking |
| **Track request** | Own status labels in words (Received, Under review, …); withdraw when allowed | Other people's requests; owner private notes; performance language |
| **Graduation / self-check** | Owners, access, who involved, what not assumed, review date; consult optional | Checkbox-only "done"; celebration theater; team ranking |
| **Errors** | What happened + what to try next (retry, Ask, Resources, Request a consultation, contact support channel) | Stack traces, agent IDs, model names, "hallucination" |
| **Empty states** | Why empty + one clear next action | Blame; "no data from the model"; icon-only void |

**No-icons rule (all routes):** Every control, status, and navigation item has a visible text label. Icons are not used in staff-facing UI.

---

## 6. Sample microcopy (before → after)

| 9 | "Congratulations! Equity badge unlocked 🎉" | "Self-check: owners and next review date filled? If yes, save your practice notes." |
| 10 | "Model hallucinated; try again" | "We don't have an approved source for that. Try Resources, or prepare a consult request." |
| 11 | "Rank my team's equity maturity" | "We don't score or rank people. You can use tools and learning paths for your own work." |

# One DHS PAC — TRD: Adaptive Program Intelligence and Agent Framework

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Document | Technical Requirements Document (standalone section) |
| Product | One DHS People, Access and Culture — Adaptive Program Intelligence |
| Version | 0.1 (engineer-ready draft) |
| Date | September 4, 2026 |
| Status | Proposed — merge candidate for full TRD |
| Parent | Product PRD v2.1 §7.1 / §10 / §11 |
| Companions | Ask MVP Contract; Community Intelligence MVP Contract; Agentic Tools Catalog; Consultation Intake & Queue; Graduation Paths |
| Staff brand | One DHS Support / resource program (not a personal chatbot) |
| Practice owner | Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant (Gary Banks) |
| Architecture pattern | Dispatcher + specialist agents + tools + governed memory + human gates |

---

## 1. Scope and relationship to PRD / tool catalog / contracts

### 1.1 What this TRD covers

This document specifies the **control plane** for Adaptive Program Intelligence: model registry, provider adapters, agent definitions, tool adapters, governed memory, evaluation harness, feature flags, autonomy enforcement, security/egress, and observability.

It implements PRD expectations that the intelligence layer can improve as models and tools improve **without rewriting staff routes**, while remaining ambitious inside bounded workflows and hard safety gates.

### 1.2 What this TRD does not cover

| Out of scope here | Lives in |
| --- | --- |
| Staff UX copy, page IA, no-icons visual design | PRD §8; Ask/CI contracts |
| Full content inventory / Knowledge Map | Knowledge Map (companion) |
| Operating roles, cadence, partnership routines | Operating Model |
| Exhaustive tool I/O JSON schemas for every catalog row | Tools Catalog + per-adapter OpenAPI (generated from this TRD’s standards) |
| DHS enterprise system integrations | Deferred (PRD §7.3) |

### 1.3 Normative parents (do not duplicate)

| Source | Binding content for this TRD |
| --- | --- |
| PRD v2.1 §10 | Model evolution, agent definitions, evals, upgrade pathway, durable memory, tool boundaries |
| PRD v2.1 §11 | Mindset twin role; workflows (a)–(c); autonomy ladder A0–A5 |
| Agentic Tools Catalog | Agent roster, tool names, permission modes, MVP must-have set, forbidden tools |
| Ask / CI / Consultation / Graduation contracts | Intent scopes, must-pass eval IDs, A0–A2 ceilings |

### 1.4 Product principles encoded in engineering

1. **Assist, do not babysit** — scale Equity & Inclusion Operations practice; graduate staff to independent execution.
2. **Mindset twin = governed practice judgment** — internal, reviewable; never staff-facing persona/product identity.
3. **Staff brand** — One DHS Support / resource program only; no model brand names in staff UI or generated staff-facing copy.
4. **MVP autonomy A0–A2**; A3+ later with undo; **A5 owner-only**.
5. **Hard safety** — no case PII, no surveillance/ranking, no autonomous publish.

---

## 2. Architecture overview

### 2.1 Layered stack

| Layer | Responsibility | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Client** | Staff and Practice Workspace UIs; Ask; Minnesota Communities; Support/Consult; contributor editors | Plain language; no model brands; no icon-only cues |
| **API / BFF** | AuthN/Z, session, request validation, response shaping, privacy notices | Scope isolation per administration; least privilege |
| **Orchestrator (Dispatcher)** | Intent route; safety pre-gates; specialist selection; tool allowlist enforce; autonomy ceiling check | Invisible control plane — not a branded persona |
| **Agents** | Specialist workflows (Ask, CI, Librarian, A11y, Intake, Embed, Graduation, …) | Config-driven definitions; enabled flag |
| **Tool adapters** | Named tools from catalog; dry-run; idempotency; audit | Permission mode enforced before side effect |
| **Model provider adapter** | Chat/completions/embeddings behind registry; swap provider without app rewrite | Staff never see vendor/model product identity |
| **Governed memory / stores** | Work objects, decisions, versions, eval results — not chat residue | Separated environments |
| **Human approval surfaces** | Preview, edit/approve/reject, queue disposition, owner promote | Required for A2 side effects and all A3+ |

### 2.2 Mermaid — control plane

```mermaid

  subgraph Client
    UI[Staff / Practice UIs]
  end
  subgraph Edge
    BFF[API / BFF]
  end
  subgraph Control

  end
  subgraph Agents

  end

  end

### 2.3 Request path (normative)

```
Authenticated request
  → BFF (authz, privacy notice injection, schema validate)
  → Orchestrator
      → safety.* (PII / surveillance / persona / publish / Tribal)
      → resolve agent definition (enabled? version? autonomy ceiling?)
      → resolve model via registry (agent.model_setting → approved registration)
      → plan tool calls (intersect agent.tools_allowlist ∩ flag-enabled tools ∩ autonomy)
      → execute tool adapters (dry_run when required)
      → preview package to client OR human-approve gate
      → on approve: durable memory write (work object / decision)
      → audit span (redacted)
```

Do **not** collapse specialists into one unbounded chat brain.

---

## 3. Model registry requirements

Models are **product configuration**, not hard-coded constants. Staff UI never displays vendor or model product names.

### 3.1 Registry record fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model_id` | string (stable opaque) | Yes | Internal ID (e.g. `mdl_ask_primary_v3`) — not a vendor string in APIs to clients |
| `provider_id` | string | Yes | Provider adapter key |
| `provider_model_ref` | string | Yes | Provider-native model identifier (server-side only) |
| `display_name_internal` | string | Yes | Owner/ops label only |
| `purpose` | enum | Yes | `chat_reason` · `embed` · `classify` · `summarize` · `eval_judge` · other |
| `allowed_agent_ids` | string[] | Yes | Which agents may bind this model |
| `scope` | object | Yes | Environments, data classes allowed (`staff_public_corpus`, `practice_workspace`, …) |
| `cost_class` | enum | Yes | `low` · `standard` · `high` |
| `risk_class` | enum | Yes | `low` · `elevated` · `restricted` |
| `context_window` | int | Yes | Tokens (or equivalent) |
| `supports_tools` | bool | Yes | Tool-calling capability |
| `supports_json_schema` | bool | Yes | Structured output support |
| `region_policy` | string | Yes | Approved processing region notes |
| `retention_notes` | string | Yes | Provider retention posture for protected work |
| `approval_state` | enum | Yes | See §3.2 |
| `eval_suite_ids` | string[] | Yes | Suites that must pass for this purpose |
| `cost_risk_notes` | text | Yes | Human-readable tradeoffs for owner review |
| `created_at` / `updated_at` | datetime | Yes | UTC |
| `approved_by` | string | Cond. | Required when `approved` or `production` |
| `version` | semver | Yes | Registry record version |

### 3.2 Approval states

| State | Meaning | Callable in prod staff paths? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `candidate` | Registered for eval only | No |
| `eval` | Running harness | No (eval env only) |
| `sandbox` | Non-prod limited traffic | No |
| `pilot` | Flagged subset of users/admins | Only if feature flag on |
| `approved` | Cleared for enablement | Yes when agent binds it |
| `production` | Default for one or more agents | Yes |
| `hold` | Temporarily withdrawn | No |
| `rejected` | Failed eval or owner reject | No |

### 3.3 Cost / risk / scope rules

- `risk_class=restricted` models cannot process Practice Workspace payloads without owner-documented retention/region approval.
- Embedding models (`purpose=embed`) are separate registrations from chat/reason models.
- Changing `provider_model_ref` for a production binding requires upgrade pathway (§9), not silent swap.
- Cost class feeds ops dashboards only — never staff ranking.

---

## 4. Provider adapter interface

Swap models/providers **without rewriting** Client, BFF routes, or agent business logic.

### 4.1 Interface (logical)

| Method | Input | Output | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `complete(req)` | messages, tools?, response_schema?, temperature?, max_tokens?, model_id | text / structured object, usage, provider_trace_id | Uses registry to resolve provider |
| `embed(req)` | texts[], model_id | vectors[], usage | Corpus indexing + retrieve |
| `health()` | — | status, latency_ms | Degraded-mode signal |
| `estimate_cost(req)` | token estimates + model_id | cost_class hint | Optional |

### 4.2 Adapter contract requirements

| Requirement | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Opaque IDs | Clients and agents pass `model_id` only; adapter maps to `provider_model_ref` |
| Timeouts | Configurable per purpose; Orchestrator treats timeout as tool/model failure (§10) |
| Retries | Idempotent retries only for safe read-like completes; no duplicate side effects |
| Redaction | Adapter must not log full prompts containing free-text user content without redaction policy |
| Structured output | Prefer schema-constrained outputs for A2 drafts that feed tools |
| Multi-provider | ≥1 production provider adapter + ≥1 stub/fixture adapter for eval/dry-run |
| No staff brand leak | Strip/forbid model brand strings from any string destined for staff-facing responses (`plain.reading_level_check` / brand lint) |

### 4.3 Configuration

Provider credentials live in environment secrets — never in agent definitions or client bundles. Regional processing and retention documented before use with protected work (PRD §13).

---

## 5. Agent definition schema

Every agent is a versioned configuration object (PRD §10).

### 5.1 Schema fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agent_id` | string | Yes | Stable ID (e.g. `ask_concierge`) |
| `version` | semver | Yes | Definition version |
| `purpose` | string | Yes | One-paragraph job statement |
| `staff_label` | string | Yes | Workflow label if shown (never persona name) |
| `inputs_schema` | JSON Schema | Yes | Allowed input shapes |
| `outputs_schema` | JSON Schema | Yes | Allowed output shapes |
| `tools_allowlist` | string[] | Yes | Catalog tool names only |
| `model_setting` | object | Yes | `{ primary_model_id, fallback_model_id?, embed_model_id? }` |
| `autonomy_ceiling` | enum A0–A5 | Yes | Hard max; runtime enforces |
| `review_rule` | enum/object | Yes | `none_observe` · `user_chooses` · `preview_required` · `human_approve` · `owner_only` |
| `eval_suite_id` | string | Yes | Must-pass suite binding |
| `enabled` | bool | Yes | Production invocation gate |
| `feature_flag` | string | No | Additional flag key |
| `scope` | object | Yes | Roles, environments, administration constraints |
| `mindset_workflow` | enum | No | `a_classify` · `b_a11y` · `c_intake` if applicable |
| `safety_profile` | string[] | Yes | Required `safety.*` tools before run |
| `created_at` / `updated_at` | datetime | Yes | UTC |
| `change_notes` | text | Yes | Why this version |

### 5.2 Validation rules

- `tools_allowlist` ⊆ Tools Catalog; forbidden tools (§Catalog §5) rejected at register time.
- `autonomy_ceiling` ≤ environment policy (MVP global max **A2** for staff/prod agents).
- `enabled=true` requires `approval_state` of bound models ∈ {`approved`,`production`,`pilot`+flag}.
- Disabling an agent must not delete eval history or decision memory.

## 7. Tool adapter standards

Every catalog tool is implemented as a **named adapter**.

### 7.1 Required adapter properties

| Property | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `tool_name` | Exact catalog string |
| Input/output JSON Schema | Validated at BFF/Orchestrator |
| `permission_mode` | `always` · `with_preview` · `human_approve` · `owner_only` |
| `min_autonomy` | A0–A5 |
| `idempotency_key` | Required for any write / queue / memory mutation |
| `dry_run` | Supported for all A2+ side-effect adapters; returns would-be mutation |
| `timeout_ms` | Explicit |
| `audit` | Always emit redacted audit event |
| `scope_check` | Administration / role denial before mutate |

### 7.2 Idempotency

- Clients/Orchestrator supply `idempotency_key` for: intake submit, memory writes, queue status transitions, progress writes.
- Duplicate keys return the original result without double-apply.
- Read tools may omit keys.

### 7.3 Audit log fields (per invocation)

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `trace_id`, `span_id` | Correlate with observability |
| `agent_id`, `agent_version` | — |
| `tool_name` | — |
| `autonomy_level_used` | Actual, not ceiling |
| `permission_mode` | — |
| `dry_run` | bool |
| `content_ids_touched` | Canonical IDs only |
| `allowlist_hit` | bool / miss reason |
| `safety_refusal_code` | If any |
| `human_disposition` | `approve` · `edit` · `reject` · `regenerate` · null |
| `model_id` | Opaque registry ID if used |
| **Prohibited** | Raw case PII; full prohibited free-text payloads |

### 7.4 Dry-run

- Default for eval harness and for any human_approve tool before commit.
- `dry_run=true` must not persist side effects (except ephemeral preview cache with TTL and no prohibited payloads).

### 7.5 Permission mode enforcement

| Mode | Runtime |
| --- | --- |
| Always | AuthZ + allowlist + safety; still audited |
| With preview | Return draft to user; persist only on explicit confirm |
| Human approve | Designated role must approve; adapter blocks commit otherwise |
| Owner only | Program owner (or written delegate) |

---

## 8. Governed program memory

### 8.1 What is stored (durable)

| Object class | Examples | Write gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Approved decisions / dispositions | Publish/hold/reject; classification confirmations | Human approve / owner |
| Content versions & review outcomes | Canonical content ID, version, authority, review date | Content governance workflows |
| Scope rules | Administration boundaries; Tribal gate state | Owner |
| Accepted / rejected recommendations | Agent proposals and owner outcomes | Human / owner |
| Evaluation results | Suite runs, model compare, promote/hold/reject | Owner |
| Consult work objects | `ConsultRequest` + heads-up packet (scrubbed) | Staff submit + owner notes |
| Practice artifacts (user) | Checklists, maps in My Workspace | User-controlled |
| Local progress | `progress.local_*` | User; deletable |

### 8.2 What is not stored (or not as truth)

| Non-memory | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Loose chat residue as program truth | Ask transcripts ≠ durable policy; retention is open decision — never promote to Official |
| Belief profiles / intercultural “scores” | Forbidden |
| Case / medical / personnel PII | Hard refuse; do not persist |
| Cross-user conversational memory | Forbidden |
| Synthetic documentary claims about communities | Forbidden |

### 8.3 Work objects over chat

Prefer structured objects (`ConsultRequest`, classification draft, a11y review draft, practice artifact) with IDs, owners, status, and review dates. Chat UX is a **transport**, not the system of record.

### 8.4 Environment separation

Mindset-private, pilot, administration, demonstration, and future enterprise stores remain technically separated (PRD §13). Demonstration uses synthetic/local data only.

---

## 9. Evaluation harness + model upgrade pathway

### 9.1 Harness requirements

| Capability | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Suite runner | `eval.run_cases` executes fixture suites in dry-run / sandbox |
| MVP suites | ASK-E*; CI-E*; CIQ-E*; GP-E*; mindset (a)–(c) must-pass (KPI-07/12) |
| Judges | Program-task criteria: accuracy, scope adherence, plain language, a11y checks, no surveillance, human-gate respect — **not** impressiveness |
| Fixtures | Synthetic content only; no prohibited PII |
| Reports | Stored via `memory.eval_results_*`; owner-readable |
| Gate | Any must-pass failure blocks release unless owner-dated exception (Ownership/PII gates not waivable) |

### 9.2 Upgrade pathway (normative)

```
candidate → eval cases → compare → sandbox → limited pilot → monitor → promote | hold | reject
```

| Stage | Exit criteria |
| --- | --- |
| Candidate | Registry record complete; purpose/scope/cost-risk set |
| Eval | Bound suites pass thresholds; no safety refusal regressions |
| Compare | Side-by-side vs current production on same fixtures (`eval.compare_models`) |
| Sandbox | Stability, latency, cost within budget; redaction verified |
| Pilot | Feature flag; limited administrations/users; monitor refusal rates + escalation quality |
| Monitor | Error budget, safety events, human reject rate |
| Promote | Owner action → `approved`/`production` + agent `model_setting` update |
| Hold / Reject | Owner action; write `memory.rejected_rec_log`; no silent re-enable |

**A5:** Only program owner promotes behavior/content adaptations to production. Agents may **propose** (A5) into memory; never self-enable (`registry.agent_toggle` / `flags.set` owner-only).

---

## 10. Feature flags and fallback / degraded behavior

### 10.1 Flag taxonomy

| Flag class | Examples | Default MVP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent enable | Per `agent_id` | Only MVP roster on |
| Tool enable | Near-term / Later tools | Off if not must-have |
| Model pilot | `model_id` pilot binding | Off |
| Autonomy experiment | A3 reversible scheduling | **Off** |
| Surface | Admin pilots, ecosystem intelligence | Per PRD §7.2 |

Flags are owner-controlled (`flags.set` near-term). Changes audited.

### 10.2 Degraded behavior matrix

| Failure | User-visible behavior | System behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary model timeout/error | “Support is briefly limited — try again or use Resources / request a consult.” Plain language; no vendor names | Fail over to `fallback_model_id` if healthy; else disable generative draft tools; keep search/browse |
| Embeddings down | Keyword `corpus.search` only; note reduced match quality internally | Semantic retrieve short-circuit |
| Tool adapter fail | Omit that capability; offer escalate / intake | Circuit-break tool; audit error code |
| Safety service fail | **Fail closed** on PII/surveillance paths (block submit) | Do not “fail open” into processing prohibited content |
| Registry unavailable | Use last-known-good local cache of production bindings (TTL); if none, generative off | Alert ops |
| Memory write fail | Show draft still downloadable/copyable where allowed; warn not saved | Retry idempotent write; no silent success |

Generative answers must show uncertainty; never invent Official authority during degraded mode.

---

## 11. Autonomy enforcement (runtime checks A0–A5)

### 11.1 Ladder (PRD §11.3)

| Level | May do | Runtime control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A0 Observe | Read, classify, summarize, detect | No external side effect |
| A1 Recommend | Propose options | Persist only as user-visible suggestion |
| A2 Produce | Editable drafts | Preview; human edit/approve/reject/regenerate before impact |
| A3 Execute reversible | Save/route/schedule/update | Undo window, pause, activity history — **not MVP default** |
| A4 Bounded workflow | Multi-step process | Approval gates, exception review, rollback |
| A5 Propose adaptation | Candidate improvements | Owner promote only |

### 11.2 Enforcement points

1. **Agent ceiling** — Orchestrator rejects planned acts above `autonomy_ceiling`.
2. **Tool min_autonomy** — Tool cannot run if agent ceiling < tool minimum.
3. **Environment policy** — MVP global prod max = **A2** unless owner-signed exception flag.
4. **Side-effect class** — Publish/send tools non-callable by agents alone (Catalog forbidden / Later human-only).
5. **A3 undo capability check** — A3 tools refuse if undo/activity-history not configured.
6. **A5** — Write proposals to memory only; `registry.agent_toggle` requires owner.

### 11.3 MVP policy

Ask, CI, Intake, Librarian, A11y, Embed, Graduation: **A0–A2 only**.  
`calendar.schedule_reversible` and auto-publish: **disabled**.

---

## 12. Security, privacy, egress allowlists

### 12.1 Hard prohibitions (engineering)

| Prohibition | Enforcement |
| --- | --- |
| Case / eligibility / medical / personnel / complaint systems | No adapters; deny by design |
| Staff ranking / belief profiling | `safety.surveillance_refuse`; no metrics UI |
| Autonomous publish / official send | No agent path to `publish.execute` / auto email/Teams |
| Tribal Nation guidance without authority | `safety.tribal_gate`; features default off |
| Portable identity+completion telemetry exporters | Blocked |
| Private community scraping | No tools |

### 12.2 AuthZ

- Strong auth for Practice Workspace and owner registry.
- Administration scope isolation with denial tests (KPI-05).
- Least privilege on `queue.status_get` (own vs owner full queue).

### 12.3 Egress allowlists

| Egress class | MVP | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model provider | Approved endpoints only | Region/retention documented |
| Corpus / app DB | Internal | — |
| Browser fetch public | Later | Explicit domain allowlist for External—verify |
| Calendar / Graph | Later | Separate integration gate |
| Webhooks out | None by default | No silent exfil |

### 12.4 Privacy notices & detection

- Entry notices on Ask, CI, Intake (`safety.privacy_notice`).
- `safety.pii_detect` hard-stop on free-text before persist.
- Logs: refusal codes + field ids — never raw prohibited payloads.

---

## 13. Observability

### 13.1 Traces

- Distributed `trace_id` across BFF → Orchestrator → Agent → Tool → Model adapter.
- Span attributes: `agent_id`, `tool_name`, `model_id` (opaque), `autonomy_level`, `dry_run`, `safety_refusal_code`, latency, token usage.
- **Redaction:** free-text user content scrubbed or hashed; never store prohibited PII in trace backends.
- Staff-facing errors: plain language; no stack traces or vendor names.

### 13.2 Metrics (ops / owner — not ranking)

| Metric | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Must-pass suite pass rate | Release gate |
| Safety refusal counts by code | Monitor attacks/misuse + false positives |
| Human reject/edit rate on A2 drafts | Quality signal |
| Model latency / error / failover rate | Degraded mode |
| Independence proxies (aggregate) | KPI-11 — path-type aggregates only |
| Cross-admin denial test results | KPI-05 |

### 13.3 What not to observe

No employee leaderboards; no belief/compliance scores; no review links that embed prohibited payloads.

---

### 14.1 Early-2027 MUST (technical)

| Item | Done when |
| --- | --- |
| Orchestrator + safety gates | Hard refusals pass Ask/CI/CIQ/GP suites |
| Agent definitions as config | Eight MVP agents versioned; enabled flags work |
| Model registry + provider adapter | ≥1 prod binding + fixture provider; staff UI brand-free |
| MVP must-have tool adapters | Catalog §4.1 + safety micro-tools |
| Governed memory baseline | Decisions, versions, eval read, consult work objects |
| Eval harness | `eval.run_cases` for ASK/CI/CIQ/GP/mindset a–c |
| Autonomy runtime A0–A2 | A3+ tools disabled |
| Feature flags | Near-term agents/tools default off |
| Degraded fallback | Search/browse survive generative outage; safety fail-closed |
| Observability | Redacted traces + ops metrics |
| Calendar | Option A: `calendar.handoff_prep` only |

### 14.2 Later / Phase 2+

| Item | Dependency |
| --- | --- |
| A3 reversible schedule / stale flags | Undo SLA + owner sign-off |
| Eval Steward write paths, model compare UI | Owner ops capacity |
| `browser.fetch_public`, office drafts, Teams draft | Allowlists + a11y gates |
| `publish.*` human-approve chain | Owner admissibility |
| DHS system integrations | Security/privacy/legal/records decision |
| Ecosystem intelligence analytics | Charter + Tribal/privacy gates (PRD §14) |
